prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer's chest and belly at the bottom center (0.1 to 0.3 m) are brightest, followed by the wearer's extended left and right forearms (0.3 to 0.5 m) holding a paintbrush on the left and a charging smartphone on the right, both within about 0.1 to 0.2 m of each other and well within the wearer's arm's reach. Below the arms, a wooden scaffold plank and a ledge at roughly 1.0 to 1.5 m sit above a cluttered dirt ground plane (around 1.8 to 2.5 m below) scattered with paint cans, bags, and containers. Across frames 1 to 3, the wearer's right hand moves the smartphone slightly rightward from in front of the left hand while an elevated dark cloth or object at the upper left (0.4 to 0.7 m) shifts out of view; in frame 4, a second person's white-clothed lower body enters on the lower left at roughly 1.2 to 1.5 m, and in frame 5, that person approaches closer from the left, extending a bright bare right arm at about 0.3 to 0.4 m directly above the wearer's left hand to touch the top of the smartphone while their head and upper torso remain out of view to the left. Compared to the cluttered RGB image, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height tiers between the wearer's hands, the mid-level wooden supports and ledge, and the ground below, as well as the close proximity of the second person's reaching arm in frame 5. However, the depth map is unreliable along the top edge where the turquoise netting is rendered completely black as if at infinite distance, and on the paintbrush handle in frames 3 and 4, which appears overly bright and nearer than the hand gripping it.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies the camera wearer's lower torso and extended left and right arms in the foreground (0.1 to 0.5 m) as 'person' masks, positioning the held rectangular device (0.4 to 0.5 m in front of the chest) between the left hand holding a paintbrush and the right hand gripping the device's right edge. Across the five frames, the map tracks the rightward shift and counter-clockwise tilt of the held device from overlapping the left hand in frame 1 to sitting between both hands in frames 2 to 5, though the device is completely missed in frame 3 and inconsistently labeled as 'cell phone' in frames 1 and 4, 'laptop' in frame 2, and 'book' in frame 5. While this map isolates the foreground body and held object from the busy background of paint cans and dirt 1.8 to 2.5 m below, it fails to segment the paintbrush, charging cable, and most ground objects within or beyond arm's reach. It is also highly unreliable in splitting the camera wearer's single torso and arms into multiple separate 'person' instances, hallucinating labels like 'bird' on the hanging cloth in frame 2 and 'donut' on a background container in frame 3, and failing to segment the second person who approaches from the left in frames 4 and 5 and reaches an arm over the wearer's left hand to touch the phone.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons for either the camera wearer or the second person. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer's torso and both outstretched arms are visible at 0.1 to 0.5 m in the lower half of the frame, facing downward toward the paintbrush in the left hand and the smartphone in the right hand, while a second person approaches from the left in frames 4 and 5 (body at 0.8 to 1.5 m, reaching arm at 0.3 to 0.4 m) with their torso oriented rightward toward the wearer's hands and their head remaining out of view outside the left frame boundary. Both the camera wearer and the second person (by frame 5) have the smartphone and paintbrush within arm's reach at roughly 0.4 m from the camera, with the second person's bare right arm partially occluding the paintbrush and the wearer's left hand in frame 5. Because the steep top-down egocentric viewpoint truncates both individuals' heads, shoulders, and upper torsos—and because the hands are partially occluded by the phone, paintbrush, and paint stains—the pose estimator completely fails and provides no spatial information beyond what is visible in the RGB frames.
